proposal.blind_spot: The known stall reasons (barrier, long scoreboard) explain barely half the stalled cycles, so the optimizer cannot tell shared-memory reduction stalls from global-memory stalls, nor whether schedulers have any eligible warps - i.e. whether more parallelism would help at all.

rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_short_scoreboar: HIGH -> restructure shared-memory usage: pad against bank conflicts, keep reduction partials in registers/warp shuffles, reduce smem round trips and their barriers / LOW -> shared memory is innocent; remove spurious barriers or attack global-load latency instead
rationale.smsp__warps_eligible.avg.per_cycle_activ: HIGH -> parallelism is sufficient and warps are ready but undispatched; cut instruction count via vectorization/fusion/simpler addressing / LOW -> schedulers are starved with all warps stalled; raise occupancy, prefetch, add ILP, or eliminate barriers to attack latency

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:It combines a direct SM utilization/saturation signal with the explicit register-based occupancy limit, which is launch- and architecture-aware, whereas raw registers-per-thread alone is only an indirect proxy.
